pr.title: feat(local): count only Lean code lines in the merge subject delta
pr.body:
### Motivation

- Owner request, 2026-09-17 (issue #574). Since issue #557 every merge subject ends with
  a Lean line delta such as `[lean +32 -230]`. It counted *every* changed line of every
  `*.lean` file, so a docstring sweep or a commented-out block read on the commits page
  like a large code change and the bracket stopped answering the question it was added
  for. The owner asked for comment and blank lines not to count.
- Protocol: `local/protocols/issues-prs.md`, "Merge subject"; the cosmetic-by-contract
  rule of issue #557 is unchanged and now enforced in the code.

### Description

- `local/bin/pr_merge.py`: `lean_line_delta` keeps its name, signature and fallback
  contract, and is now a thin wrapper that returns `None` on **any** exception. The
  measurement behind it takes the changed blobs from
  `git diff --raw -z --find-renames --no-abbrev <merge base>...<head> -- '*.lean'` —
  blob ids rather than paths, so the two sides of a rename need no quoting rule and no
  pathological filename can derail the scan — reads added line numbers from the head
  blob's `-U0` hunk headers and removed ones from the merge-base blob's, and counts a
  line only when a per-line mask calls it code.
- New `lean_code_line_mask`: one left-to-right scan carrying a block-comment nesting
  depth. It skips line comments, block, doc and module-doc comments (`/-`, and the
  `/--` and `/-!` forms that share its `-/` closer, all nesting), and blank or
  whitespace-only lines; a line of code merely trailed by a comment still counts. It is
  naive by design about the rest of Lean's grammar: only double-quoted strings hide
  comment delimiters. Following independent review F1, ordinary string and escape
  state persist through physical newlines until the closing quote, so delimiters in a
  multiline string cannot hide later code as a false block comment.
- Added files contribute their own code lines, deleted files subtract theirs, a pure
  rename contributes none, and a blob git reports as binary contributes none.
- Unchanged: the subject format (`[lean +A -D]`, `[lean 0]` when no code line changed),
  the title sanitization and closing-keyword defusal, the REST payload keys, every gate
  and every CI step. Nothing reads the number back, and it still cannot block a merge.
- `local/protocols/issues-prs.md` states the new counting rule;
  `local/protocols/EVOLUTION.md` carries the dated entry, amended for multiline strings.

### Testing

- Original commit `723e2d2ac6783b2cfe2fea78cacd2fc6b0088874`:
  `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests -p "test_*.py"` in the worktree:
  **643 tests, OK (9 skipped)**, 133 s. `scripts/tests/test_github_workflow.py` alone:
  54 tests, OK. These results predate the F1 repair; full CI remains for MAIN.
- F1 repair: focused `MergeSubjectTests` passed (13 tests); `git diff --check`
  and `scripts/install_git_hooks.sh --check` passed. The full workflow test module
  was rerun on the repaired test file (55 tests, OK). The ordinary pre-commit
  hook passed its repository-wide unit tests (644 tests, 9 skipped).
- Cases beside the issue #557 ones in `MergeSubjectTests`: the mask over line
  comments, a nested block comment (a scanner that closed on the inner `-/` would
  mislabel the rest of that line *and* every line after it), doc and module-doc
  comments, code with a trailing comment, blank and whitespace-only lines, and a string
  holding comment delimiters; then the delta over a modified file, an added file
  (prose-only beside a one-theorem module), a deleted file, a rename with added code,
  and two fallback paths — an `OSError` from git and a malformed raw record, both
  yielding `None` rather than raising. The F1 repair adds a delta regression where a
  later theorem changes after a multiline string containing `/-` (expect `[lean +1 -1]`)
  and a mask check for an escaped quote in a continued string. The escaped-quote example
  was accepted by `lake env lean --stdin`; the original multiline literal was already
  checked by the independent reviewer.
- Dry run over real merge commits on `main`, old figure vs new (original commit):
  - `Merge PR #460: refactor(QPBT): Align subline names and conditional statements`
    — old `[lean +82 -72]`, new `[lean +36 -36]`.
  - `Merge pull request #453 from Dengnifer/issue-450-nondegenerate-pasting-mass`
    — old `[lean +32 -230]`, new `[lean +24 -193]`.
  - `Merge pull request #432 from Dengnifer/issue-429-affine-evaluation`
    — old `[lean +3 -1]`, new `[lean 0]`: that packet moved comment lines only.
- No Lean file changes in this PR, so the Lean build and proof-integrity surface is
  untouched; the workflow-layer CI steps run because `local/bin` and `local/protocols`
  changed. MAIN will rerun exact-head CI and request an independent review.

---

Closes #574
